studies.name: Rule of Thirds
studies.principle: Focal mass at intersection, secondary balance, accent hierarchy

studies.name: Dynamic Diagonal
studies.principle: Diagonal energy creates movement, masses build rhythm along the line

studies.name: Balance Study
studies.principle: One heavy mass can balance multiple lighter ones through visual weight distribution

studies.name: 5-Value Scale
studies.principle: All visual information compresses to 5 values. Master value before color.

studies.name: Notan Design
studies.principle: Strong compositions work as pure light/dark interlocking shapes

studies.name: Value Hierarchy
studies.principle: Darkest darks and lightest lights near focal point. Background lighter, foreground darker.

studies.name: Color Temperature
studies.principle: Warm advances, cool recedes. Temperature contrast creates depth without value change.

studies.name: Complementary Harmony
studies.principle: Complementary pairs create maximum chromatic contrast. Use one as dominant, one as accent.

studies.name: Limited Palette
studies.principle: 3 colors force intentional choices. Limitation breeds coherence and sophistication.

studies.name: Geometric vs Organic
studies.principle: Shape language defines character personality before detail. Angular = mechanical/fierce. Rounded = natural/friendly.

studies.name: Shape Personality
studies.principle: Silhouette alone communicates personality. Proportions carry emotional weight.

studies.name: Shape Rhythm
studies.principle: Repetition with variation creates visual rhythm. Size, spacing, and position variation prevent monotony.

studies.name: Edge Hierarchy
studies.principle: Hard edges attract attention. Soft edges recede. Lost edges merge. Control edge sharpness to direct the eye.

studies.name: Edge Types
studies.principle: Edge quality is a design choice. Hard = defined, Soft = atmospheric, Lost = mystery/depth.

studies.name: Edge for Focal Control
studies.principle: One hard edge among soft edges instantly draws the eye. The sharpest edge wins attention.

studies.name: Material Value Patterns
studies.principle: Each material has a characteristic value pattern: metal=high contrast, fabric=soft, wood=directional, glass=transparent

studies.name: Material through Marks
studies.principle: Mark-making defines material: brush=painterly, geometric=vector, noise=procedural

studies.name: Material Light Response
studies.principle: Material is defined by how it responds to light: chrome=reflective, matte=diffuse, emissive=self-lit, transparent=transmissive
